scheme_name: Central Glass & Ceramic Research Institute (CGCRI) Incubation
overview: The Central Glass & Ceramic Research Institute (CGCRI) Incubation program supports startups and entrepreneurs in the glass and ceramics sector by providing access to advanced research facilities, technical expertise, and infrastructure for product development and innovation. The initiative aims to foster entrepreneurship, promote technology transfer, and strengthen the industrial base in glass and ceramics through incubation support and collaborative R&D.
objectives: To provide incubation support to startups and entrepreneurs in glass and ceramics
To facilitate access to CGCRI's research infrastructure and technical expertise
To promote innovation and technology development in glass and ceramic materials
To enable product prototyping, testing, and validation for market readiness
To encourage industry-academia collaboration and knowledge transfer
To support the growth of MSMEs in the glass and ceramics sector
eligibility: Startups, entrepreneurs, and MSMEs engaged in innovative activities related to glass and ceramics, including material development, product design, and process improvement, are eligible to apply for incubation support at CGCRI.
benefits: Incubatees gain access to CGCRI's state-of-the-art laboratories, pilot plants, characterization facilities, and technical mentorship. Benefits include support for R&D, prototype development, testing and validation, technology transfer, and guidance on intellectual property rights and regulatory compliance.
financial_support: Financial support under the incubation program-specific funding for not detailed in the evidence. No direct financial grant is mentioned. support is primarily in-kind, technical services).
application_process: 1. Submit a proposal detailing the innovative idea, objectives, and expected outcomes in glass and ceramics. 2. Undergo technical and feasibility evaluation by CGCRI experts. 3. If selected, sign an incubation agreement outlining terms of engagement. 4. Commence work under mentorship with access to CGCRI facilities. 5. Progress is monitored periodically, and support continues based on milestones.
required_documents: Any existing IP or prior work details
implementing_agency: Central Glass & Ceramic Research Institute (CGCRI), Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
caveats: Incubation support is subject to availability of facilities and technical expertise
Continued support depends on performance and progress evaluation
Intellectual property arising from joint work may be governed by CSIR guidelines
